name: Acid Chrome
fit: Launches, music & nightlife, loud personal brands
keywords: y2k chrome rave flyer neon nightlife
idea: The page is a Y2K rave flyer. Liquid-chrome display type tilts to catch the light, an acid-green grid floor runs to the horizon, and the details read like a line-up.
note: Live: move the pointer across the stage. The chrome headline tilts in 3D and its specular highlight follows you; the grid floor never stops running.
borrowed: Late-90s/Y2K rave and club flyers: liquid-chrome logotypes, acid smileys and acid-green, wireframe horizon grids, rotating sticker roundels, line-ups set in wide grotesks, and the photocopied "info line" at the bottom.
mood: Loud, nocturnal, euphoric. Suits product launches, event and music sites, creative-tech personal brands, and any page whose job is hype. One screen of maximum energy, then calm down for the reading parts.

type.meta: Display · Unbounded 900, -0.06em, chrome gradient + magenta extrude
Info line · IBM Plex Mono, tracked +0.18em

motion: Pointer → `--mx/--my` → `rotateX/Y` on the title, plus a radial highlight layer that slides across the chrome.
Floor: `rotateX(70deg)` plane whose background-position loops every 900ms.
Sticker text rides an SVG `textPath` and spins once every 9s.
watchouts: Chrome text is decoration. Keep it to 2–4 words and never for anything that must be read quickly.
No strobes. Real flyers flash; web pages must not (WCAG 2.3.1).
Acid on void is fine for labels; body copy goes in near-white.
